note: Common dashboard warning lights (ISO 2575 style symbols). Red: stop safely. Amber: get it checked soon. Green or blue: information. Symbols and colours vary between cars: the owner's manual is the reference.

lights.name: Engine oil pressure
lights.meaning: The engine's oil pressure is too low. Running the engine like this can destroy it within minutes.
todo: Stop safely and switch the engine off at once.
When the engine has cooled, check the oil level with the dipstick.
Don't drive with this light on, even if the level looks right: call roadside assistance.

lights.name: Engine temperature
todo: Stop safely and switch the engine off.
Don't open the radiator or coolant cap while the engine is hot: it can spray boiling coolant.
Wait at least 30 minutes, then check the coolant level. Call roadside assistance if it's low or the light returns.

lights.name: Brake system
lights.meaning: The parking brake is on, or the brake fluid is low or the brake system has a fault.
todo: Release the parking brake fully.
If the light stays on, stop safely and don't drive: brakes may not work properly. Call roadside assistance.

lights.name: Battery charging
lights.meaning: The battery isn't being charged (alternator or drive belt). The car will stop when the battery runs down.
todo: Switch off the AC, music and other loads.
Drive only to the nearest workshop, or stop safely and call roadside assistance.
If the steering also gets heavy or the temperature rises, the drive belt may be broken: stop at once.

lights.name: Airbag
lights.meaning: The airbag system has a fault: the airbags may not open in a crash.
todo: The car can be driven, but get it checked as soon as possible.
Don't fit seat covers that cover the side airbags in the seats.

lights.name: Power steering
lights.meaning: The power steering has a fault. Steering may become very heavy.
todo: Hold the wheel firmly and drive slowly to a safe place.
If steering is heavy, don't continue: call roadside assistance.

lights.name: Electric drive system
lights.meaning: The electric drive or high-voltage battery has a fault.
todo: Stop safely and switch the car off.
Call roadside assistance; don't try to repair anything on the high-voltage system.
If you see smoke or smell burning, get everyone out and away from the car and call 112.

lights.name: Check engine
lights.meaning: The engine or emissions system has detected a fault.
todo: Steady light: drive gently and get it checked soon.
Flashing light: misfiring that can damage the catalytic converter. Slow down, avoid hard acceleration and get it checked now.
Check the fuel cap is closed properly; a loose cap can turn it on.

lights.name: ABS
lights.meaning: The anti-lock braking system isn't working. Normal braking still works, but wheels can lock in hard braking.
todo: Drive carefully, keep more distance and get it checked soon.
If the red brake light is on too, stop safely and don't drive.

lights.name: Stability control (ESP)
lights.meaning: Flashing while driving: the system is working on a slippery road. Steady: the system is switched off or has a fault.
todo: Flashing: ease off the accelerator and drive gently.
Steady: switch it on again (button with the same symbol and OFF); if it stays on, get it checked.

lights.name: Tyre pressure
lights.meaning: One or more tyres are under-inflated, or blinking first: the tyre pressure system has a fault.
todo: Stop when safe and look at the tyres.
Fill to the pressure on the door-frame sticker and reset the system if your car needs it.

lights.name: Collision warning or emergency braking off
lights.meaning: Forward collision warning or automatic emergency braking is switched off or unavailable (blocked sensor, bad weather or a fault).
todo: Check whether it was switched off in the driver-assistance settings.
Clean the camera area of the windscreen and the radar sensor.

lights.name: Diesel pre-heating
todo: Wait until it goes out, then start.
If it flashes while driving, the engine has a fault: get it checked.

lights.name: Diesel particulate filter
lights.meaning: The exhaust filter is getting full and needs to clean itself.
todo: Drive at a steady speed above about 60 km/h for 15 to 20 minutes, for example on a highway.
If it stays on, get it checked before the engine reduces power.

lights.name: Low fuel
lights.meaning: Fuel is low (usually 5 to 8 litres left).
todo: Refuel soon. Running a car dry can damage the fuel pump.

lights.name: Seat belt
todo: Everyone, front and rear, should wear a seat belt.
